correctness.rationale: Fourier orthogonality gives the exact correlation-fiber formula. The difference-set axiom fixes every nonzero fiber size at lambda. Cauchy--Schwarz on each fiber, followed by the exact identity sum B_g=S^2-Q and Q>=S^2/k, proves the bound. Keeping both remainders gives the displayed deficit identity. The equality conditions are exactly the equality conditions in these two inequalities. Constant coefficients attain the bound, so the constant is sharp. The standalone exact-arithmetic verifier replays the identity and sharpness on three independent cyclic examples.

value.rationale: Difference sets are canonical exact-uniform additive designs and finite Fourier extension is a standard harmonic-analysis invariant. The result converts their defining difference uniformity into an exact sharp L2-to-L4 constant for arbitrary coefficients, and the deficit separates the two mathematically meaningful loss mechanisms: amplitude nonuniformity and phase decoherence inside difference fibers. This is a reusable structural statement rather than a one-off numerical evaluation.
